export_controls.text:
My Chip Security Act would require advanced AI chips to include hardware that allows us to track where they are and how they are being used. 

Congress should pass this legislation as a first step toward implementing technically feasible safeguards against the risks posed by advanced AI.

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges Congress to pass his Chip Security Act requiring hardware tracking of advanced AI chips.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly backs hardware tracking of advanced AI chips as a safeguard.

export_controls.text:
Anyone who has read METR's Technical Report on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident will understand that software-only controls will not be sufficient to contain superhuman AI.

Any continuing work on adversarial superhuman intelligence must rely on the physical containment methods used for nuclear security: including air gap isolation, data diodes, and a two-person rule for data exfiltration.

Moreover, the internet itself must be hardened against penetration by self-propagating AI agents: no more untraceable access to high-end AI computing facilities, and no anonymous fund aggregation or payments.

The first useful step is our Chip Security Act, currently included in the Senate NDAA.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls the Chip Security Act a first step and backs traceability for high-end AI computing access.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Support for chip tracking is explicit, but the link to overseas export controls is indirect.

astra.reason: He advocates AI containment and traceable computing access without connecting these measures or the Chip Security Act to overseas access.
astra.confidence_reason: The statement specifies security measures but supplies no export-related purpose or geographic restriction.

export_controls.text:
Trump and Commerce Secretary @howardlutnick may have allowed hundreds of thousands of advanced American AI chips to be used by China over the past year and a half.

I hope to see them do more than close a loophole to correct their negligence, but the damage is already done. Congress must pass my Chip Security Act to prevent China from further benefiting from American AI chips and undermining our technological advantages.

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges Congress to pass his Chip Security Act to stop China from benefiting from American AI chips.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly calls for passing his act to block China's use of US AI chips.

export_controls.text:
Thrilled that my Chip Security Act with @RepHuizenga, @RepMoolenaar, and @CongressmanRaja passed through committee! 

This is an important—and bipartisan—step to prevent powerful AI technology from getting into the wrong hands.

deepseek.reason: The speaker celebrates his Chip Security Act as a step to prevent powerful AI technology from reaching wrong hands, endorsing tighter access restrictions.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement clearly supports restricting access to powerful AI technology, but the exact export-control scope of the named bill is not spelled out.

astra.reason: He endorses the Chip Security Act but does not describe restrictions or enforcement on overseas AI access.
astra.confidence_reason: The bill's name and general security objective do not establish its export provisions within the supplied evidence.

As Congress’ chip designer, AI programmer, and PhD physicist, I know that we have the technical tools to prevent powerful AI technology from getting into the wrong hands.

That's why I'm leading the bipartisan effort to protect our chip exports from being smuggled into China. Read more: 

https://t.co/yTTlpytsOs

deepseek.reason: The speaker says he is leading a bipartisan effort to protect chip exports from being smuggled into China.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly endorses anti-smuggling enforcement for chip exports to China.

export_controls.text: Artificial intelligence is coming at us, and we are not ready for it. [...] The first country that gets what amounts to an artificial general intelligence (AGI), this is an ability to simply—an artificial intelligence agent that can outperform humans in most things.
export_controls.context: House hearing examining policies to counter China, focusing on AI competition and export controls.

deepseek.confidence_reason: The text discusses AI competition readiness, not export restrictions or enforcement.

export_controls.text: As a PhD physicist and chip designer who first programmed neural networks at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory in the 1990s, I’ve been tracking the exponential growth of AI capabilities for decades, and I’m pleased Congress is beginning to take action on this issue.
